sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French codified system; commercial registration and corporate governance governed by the Code de commerce; judicial precedent persuasive but not binding)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: DTA France-China on income and capital gains taxation, signed 26 November 2013, in force 28 December 2014 (avoidance of double taxation and fiscal evasion)
BIT France-China on the reciprocal promotion and protection of investments, signed 26 November 2004, in force 1 January 2007
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI), signed 30 December 2020; ratification frozen and not in force, not a legally operative basis for investor protection
France-US DTA and Protocol, signed 1994, as amended including 2006/2009 protocols, in force and operative

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 et seq. as transposing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; CMF Articles L.561-45 to L.561-57 and Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 governing the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); Article L.561-46 (threshold), Article L.561-10 (PEP due diligence); Decree No. 2024-813 of 25 July 2024 restricting consultation of the RBE to authorities, regulated professions and legitimate-interest applicants following the CJEU joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; implementing Arrêtés of the Ministère de l'Économie (asset-freeze lists); registration of the RBE is effected jointly with the RCS filing via the INPI Guichet unique.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE is no longer publicly searchable as of 1 August 2024; access is limited to judicial authorities, TRACFIN, ACPR, notaries, legal professionals and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; UBO names and holdings remain on file for the life of the company and for 5 years post-liquidation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and current constitutional documents (articles of association, certificate of continuance if applicable) of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's country of origin (e.g. Companies Registry Hong Kong, SAMR/AMKR mainland China, Companies House UK)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961; France and the shareholder's origin state must both be contracting parties; Consular Legalization only if origin state is non-Apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (attestation de dépôt des comptes / certificate of incumbency) of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or licensed company registry agent in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the French SARL, the execution of the statutory deed, and the appointment/powers of the gérant (managing director)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / corporate secretary of the corporate shareholder, authenticated by notarial certification in the origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney of the legal representative or designated manager (gérant) for filing formalities, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport of the designated gérant (individual natural person serving as statutory manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the issuer's home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Consular Legalization if the origin state is not a Party to the Hague Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all natural and legal persons (shareholders, gérant, authorized representatives) against: (i) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and UN Security Council consolidated lists; (ii) French national asset-freeze files issued by the Ministère de l'Économie (gel des avoirs); (iii) PEP designation under CMF Article L.561-10, requiring enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs residing outside France; (iv) OFAC/HLCAF restrictions only where USD settlement or payment routing touches the United States payment system (mitigated for the target payment rails Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments, which centrally apply sanctions filtering). All screening evidence must be retained in the AML/KYC file for at least 5 years after the close of the business relationship (CMF Article L.561-12-2). Because the business scope is low-risk standard e-commerce retail (ISIC 4791, NAICS 458110), standard client due diligence (CDD) applies; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered by any UBO/PEP exposure, opaque corporate chain, or origin from a FATF-monitored jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Official French business formalities platform 'Le Guichet Unique' operated by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; company name and business availability search via Infogreffe.fr (RCS extracts) and trademark search via data.inpi.fr (INPI BOPI database)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet and must be pronounceable/definable in French; foreign words are permitted but must be indicated in the statutes with a French transliteration if necessary. The name must not create confusion with an existing local business name or registered trademark, must not include the legal form suffix of another company type (e.g. 'SA', 'SAS', 'EURL') unless the entity is actually of that form, and must not be contrary to public order or good morals (Article L.123-1 of the Code de commerce). For a fast-fashion e-commerce brand, a distinct word mark or invented term is recommended to ensure availability across the Benelux and EU trademark registries as well.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Banquier / Crédit / Financement / Caisse — reserved for regulated credit institutions (prior ACPR authorization mandatory)
Assurance / Réassurance / Courtier d'assurance — reserved for regulated insurance intermediaries (prior ACPR authorization mandatory)
Ministère / Préfecture / Mairie / République / National / Départemental / Municipal — terms implying state or public-law affiliation (express administrative authorization required)
SARL / SA / SAS / SNC — legal-form tokens that must correspond exactly to the actual corporate form of the entity; misleading use is prohibited
Names of protected geographic appellations, national emblems, or famous trademarks without prior consent of the rightholder
Terms contrary to public order or good morals (Article L.123-1 of the Code de commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a statutory advance name-reservation system; name protection is obtained upon filing of the statutes and RCS registration. If the Guichet unique / registrar (greffier du tribunal de commerce) rejects the proposed name, the applicant must: (i) receive a written reasoned refusal (décision motivée); (ii) amend the corporate name in the draft statutes and re-submit the full filing via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr with a corrected name; or (iii) file a formal appeal (contestation du refus) before the President of the Tribunal de commerce (or Tribunal judiciaire) within 15 days from notification of the refusal, in accordance with Article R.123-152 of the Code de commerce. A simultaneous administrative complaint may also be sent to the INPI's Guichet unique support team for procedural error. Re-filing after a name conflict typically takes 3-5 business days; a trademark opposition or civil action in tort (concurrence déloyale) is available against a bad-faith conflicting name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restrictively permissible. A SARL must have a real and verifiable registered office (siège social) in France (Code de commerce Article L.123-25). Domiciliation at the gérant's private residence is allowed for a maximum of five years (Code de commerce Article L.123-11-1), subject to local land-use law. Alternatively, a licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) may be used under Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-166 et seq., provided the provider is declared and the contract is in writing. A pure virtual mailbox without structural reception and handling capacity is not legally sufficient; the address must be a genuine place of business administration and verifiable for tax, URSSAF and BODACC purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Moderate for a low-risk e-commerce entity: unannounced on-site verification by DGFiP (tax authority) or URSSAF (social security) occurs on a risk-based target, with estimated probability of approximately 10-12% during the first 12 months of trading; documentary KYC/AML controls and tax registration verifications approach 100%. If the entity is domiciliated with a non-licensed provider or the registered office cannot be evidenced, inspection likelihood rises sharply (estimated over 75% in enforcement sweeps).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal publication of the incorporation notice in an authorized legal gazette (annonce légale) at the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (authorized legal announcements gazette in the department of the siège social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff per line (unified national price cap since 1 July 2016); approximate EUR 230 inclusive of publication tax

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the INPI Guichet unique, including the declaration of beneficial owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (court registry) / INPI (Guichet unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for capital-company registrations set by decree; approximately EUR 79 per SARL creation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / commercial domiciliation service of a licensed provider — 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed private domiciliation company (société de domiciliation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark tarif: EUR 50-80 per month including mail handling, legal address, and KYC/ADR acceptance documentation; estimated EUR 600 for 12 months

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of apostilled corporate documents of the foreign shareholder (5-8 pages bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-registered certified translator (expert assermenté près la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 30-50 per page; estimated EUR 150 for 5 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille legalization fees for foreign corporate documents (4-5 documents in the country of origin of the corporate shareholder)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the origin state (e.g. Companies Registry, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or designated local authority)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fee in origin jurisdiction (typically USD 10-50 per document, depending on the competent authority); estimated USD 60 for 4 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate law firm / incorporation agent professional fees: drafting of statutes (statuts), corporate resolutions, KYC/AML review, UBO declaration and filing supervision
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French corporate law firm (Avocat au Barreau) or regulated fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat-fee for a standard SARL incorporation: EUR 700-1,200; estimated EUR 900

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Optional registration of the fast-fashion brand as a French trademark (INPI e-filing, one class, covering online retail and apparel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: INPI official statutory fee of EUR 190 per class for electronic filing; estimated USD 206 at prevailing EUR/USD exchange rate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.123-1 et seq. (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) and L.223-1 through L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Civil Code Article 1832; Décret n° 84-406 of 30 April 1984 on RCS formalities; implementing rules on the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (court registry maintaining the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), operated through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises administered by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de société à responsabilité limitée and CERFA M0 declaration (demande d'immatriculation au RCS), submitted electronically via the INPI Guichet Unique portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: French law sets no statutory minimum capital for a SARL. Cash subscriptions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account opened in the name of the company in formation with a French credit institution or notary; the depositary issues a capital-deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) that must be attached to the RCS application. The articles may provide that only one-fifth of cash quotas is paid up at subscription, with the remaining balance callable within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the associates of the company in formation, as follows: (1) The draft articles of association are adopted verbatim, creating a Société à Responsabilité Limitée under the name [Company] SARL. (2) The share capital of €[...] is subscribed in full by the undersigned associates in the proportions stated in the articles, and the cash subscriptions remain deposited in a blocked account until registration, in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code. (3) The registered office of the company is fixed at [registered-office address], France. (4) [Surname, Given Name] is hereby appointed sole manager (gérant) for an indefinite term with full power of management and representation. (5) The manager is authorized to publish the legal notice, complete the RCS application, and take every action necessary to obtain the K-bis registration and commence the e-commerce activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and signature of the SARL articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The associates, assisted where appropriate by a French notary; final electronic lodgment through the INPI Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language statutes containing the corporate name, corporate object (electronic retailing of fast-fashion apparel and footwear), registered office or domiciliation agreement, duration of 99 years, share capital and quota allocation, rights attaching to shares, transfer restrictions, decision rules, and appointment of the gérant. Ensure that all associates sign the final articles and that the gérant signs a formal acceptance of office. If any contribution in kind is made, appoint a commissaire aux apports; otherwise, restrict the articles to cash contributions only.
required_dossiers: Draft statutes / statuts in French
Passport or national identity document of each associate
Proof of residential address of each associate
Formal acceptance of office signed by the gérant
Draft beneficial owner declaration (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or the Guichet Unique queries the corporate object clause or the registered office proof, amend the statutes or provide a corrected lease/domiciliation certificate and resubmit the same dossier through the portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of cash capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French licensed credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company in formation and transfer the cash subscriptions subscribed by each associate. Obtain a capital-deposit certificate from the depositary stating the exact amount deposited, the account reference, the date, and the fact that the funds are blocked for the benefit of the company until registration. The certificate must be issued in the exact legal name of the SARL and must accompany the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Subscription list / état des souscriptions et versements
Signed articles of association
Identity documents of the associates making payments
Capital-deposit certificate / attestation de dépôt des fonds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the escrow account because of a mismatch in the company name or corporate object, supply a corrected copy of the draft statutes or the Guichet Unique filing reference; if the certificate is defective, obtain an amended certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the formation notice in a legal announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An approved legal announcements journal (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office; the insertion may be arranged from the Guichet Unique portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish the constitution notice (avis de constitution) containing the mandatory particulars: legal form, company name, capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, names of managers, and the RCS court with which registration will be requested. Obtain the publication certificate (justificatif d'annonce légale), as it must be filed with the application to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Final text of the formation notice
Signed articles of association
Identity details of the gérant(s)
Publication certificate issued by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is published with an omission or typographical error, publish a corrective notice and submit both the original and corrective notices; if the registry rejects the initial notice as fundamentally invalid, arrange a second full publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the complete incorporation dossier through Guichet Unique / INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI), which transmits the dossier to the Greffe du tribunal de commerce, INSEE, URSSAF, and the relevant fiscal authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the official formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr portal, select creation of a SARL, and complete the M0 declaration data. Attach the signed statutes, capital-deposit certificate, publication certificate, proof of registered office (lease, landlord attestation, or approved domiciliation agreement), identity and non-condemnation declaration of the gérant, and the beneficial owner declaration. Pay the applicable RCS registry fees and retain the acknowledgement of receipt with a unique dossier number.
required_dossiers: Signed CERFA M0 declaration
Certified or original PDF of the articles of association
Capital-deposit certificate / attestation de dépôt des fonds
Legal publication certificate / justificatif d'annonce légale
Proof of registered office (lease, title, landlord attestation, or domiciliation agreement)
Identity document of the gérant
Gérant's declaration on honour of absence of disqualification
Beneficial ownership declaration / RBE form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INPI issues a notice of incomplete dossier, access the dossier identified in the notice, supply the missing attachments within the prescribed period, and resubmit; if the prescribed period expires, a new formation formalité may be filed with the corrected set of documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, INSEE identification, and issuance of K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce in the jurisdiction of the registered office; INSEE generates the SIREN/SIRET numbers and the APE/NAF code.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The court registry verifies the statutory compliance of the dossier and registers the SARL in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés. Upon registration, the company obtains the RCS registration number, SIREN, SIRET, and the APE/NAF code corresponding to the e-commerce retail activity. The registry then issues the K-bis extract, which is the official proof of legal personality and existence of the company.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique acknowledgement of receipt
INPI submission reference number
All statutory attachments already lodged in the formation dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe refuses registration, first submit an informal rectification request to the greffe; if the refusal persists, appeal to the president of the tribunal de commerce in summary proceedings or file a new corrected application.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), operating through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and the Direction Régionale des Douanes et Droits Indirects for VAT operational matters; online portals: impots.gouv.fr, professionnels.impots.gouv.fr, and the EU-required national VAT registration platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign SARL or branch obtains a French tax identity (SIREN, SIRET and Numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) by completing the national online registration procedure via le-guichet.fr or, for non-established taxable persons, the specific VAT registration form 'MISE-ANA' filed with the SIE compétent. For a resident SARL, the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce issues the SIREN on incorporation, after which the SIE assigns the VAT number upon fulfilment of the tax regime election. Non-resident sellers performing distance sales into France must register directly for French VAT before the first taxable supply; no minimum turnover exemption applies to non-resident operators, and for intra-EU distance sales the €10,000 EU-wide Union threshold determines whether French VAT registration is triggered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A French SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) under Article 206(1) CGI on its worldwide profits, and does not enjoy pass-through treatment under national law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in France. Available statutory mechanics include: (i) election for a 'SARL de famille' to be taxed under the personal income tax regime (Impôt sur le Revenu, IR) if all shares are held by relatives (CGI art. 239 and 239 bis AA); (ii) election for French consolidated tax grouping under CGI art. 223 A et seq.; (iii) optional territoriality election for qualifying French permanent establishments of non-resident corporations; (iv) the hybrid mismatch election framework under the ATAD/BEPS transposition rules requiring corresponding foreign-tax analysis; and (v) no separate check-the-box regime is available for US-style entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 91,900 annual taxable turnover for sales of goods and goods-related services; EUR 36,800 for other services (franchise en base thresholds under current Finance Law). The franchise is not available to non-resident taxable persons, and intra-EU distance sales of goods become subject to French VAT once the aggregate annual distance sales into France exceed EUR 10,000 or upon voluntary registration; no threshold applies for B2C imports of fast-fashion goods where the fiscal representation rules for e-commerce platforms apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory B2B e-invoicing and B2C e-reporting under a phased timeline: large and mid-sized enterprises are required to comply from 1 September 2026, and all other businesses from 1 September 2027. E-invoices must be transmitted in a structured format (EN 16931) through a certified Partenaire de Dématérialisation (PDP) or the public 'Chorus Pro' portal. No real-time fiscal stamp is affixed in France; instead, transaction data is transmitted periodically to DGFiP via PDP-to-administration APIs. The regime will include invoice exchange at C3PS/PPAD levels, with data provided to the AIF (Archivage, Instruction et Flux) system. Non-compliant e-invoicing attracts penalties under CGI art. 289 and administrative fines, including rejection of deduction or refund claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of fast-fashion apparel and footwear physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union qualify for the 0% export VAT rate under CGI art. 262-I-1°. The SARL must prove both the physical removal of goods from EU territory (within a maximum period of 90 days from delivery, unless justified) and the transport at the purchaser's risk and responsibility. Directly linked services, such as freight, handling or export-related processing supplied after export commission, may also be zero-rated under CGI art. 262-II-2°, provided the services are immediately connected to the export transaction and performed for the exporter or the non-resident customer. No further value added in France before export is permitted; extra-Community export through a customs warehouse or via an e-commerce logistics platform requires customs status 'export' and the legitimate export frontier evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation issued via DELTA / Z.008 or the simplified export procedure known as Z.009 or C&P process)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / Sea Waybill evidencing physical removal from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment confirmation proving that export proceeds are received from a non-French source and are reconciliated with bank outflows
Commercial Invoice relevant to the exported goods, including EAN/SKU, quantities, and CN8 codes
Proof of transport buyer's risk subsidence (e.g., Incoterms clause) where applicable
Intrastat declaration for intra-EU dispatch (if the goods are supplied to a foreign ERP customer within the EU, though that is exempt not zero-rated)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and Customs exercise heightened scrutiny of e-commerce exporters to verify the correlation between customs files, logistic events and bank receipts. Any misrepresentation of export evidence or abusive use of zero-rating, including forged bills of lading, fictitious inward remittances, or failure to repatriate foreign-currency proceeds within the 180-day statutory deadline, triggers immediate assessment of French VAT at the standard rate of 20.0%. Legal mechanisms include the 40% bad-faith penalty under CGI art. 1729(a), the 80% penalty for manipulation or dissimulation under CGI art. 1729(b), plus monthly interest of 0.5% under CGI art. 1734. Criminal liability under CGI art. 1741 and Code des Douanes art. 414 may subject directors to imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to EUR 500,000, with the company exposed to the enhanced corporate fine of EUR 2,000,000 in serious customs fraud. The general tax audit reprise period is three years under Livre des Procédures Fiscales art. L169, extended to six years where fraudulent conduct is established, allowing DGFiP to claw back past zero-rating benefits for the full extension period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) as the national central bank and monetary authority; ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as the integrated prudential and AML/CFT supervisor of credit institutions and payment services providers; Direction Générale du Trésor within the French Ministry of Economy and Finance as overseer of the external financial relations regime. Operational regulation is embedded in the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF) Books I through V and the PSD2 transposition (ordonnance n° 2017-1252).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for the euro as regards the current account (receipts for fast-fashion e-commerce sales, refunds, logistics payments, platform fees) and the capital account (equity injections, profit distribution), subject to the general free movement of capital rule under Article 63 TFEU and CMF Article L151-2. No prior administrative licence is required for capital inflows into a non-regulated retail distribution business. Inward foreign direct investment in ISIC 4791 (e-commerce of apparel, NAICS 458110) is not a 'dual-use' or sensitive sector under Decree No. 2023-1294, so the acquisition or constitution of the SARL by a non-resident shareholder is only subject to the ex-post statistical declaration regime. Dividends to an EU/EEA parent are exempt from withholding under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) plus the French domestic participation threshold of 5% and the two-year holding condition (Articles 145 and 216 CGI); dividends to non-EU residents are subject to withholding under Article 119-2 CGI (generally 30% for non-cooperative states, reduced by treaty to 15% or less, or by domestic rules) unless an applicable tax treaty grants a lower rate. Residual hurdles are documentary, not prohibitive: (i) annual balance-of-payments (BoP) reporting obligations where cross-border flows exceed the thresholds set by the Banque de France decree of 12 February 1987, as updated, (ii) attestations of distributable profits per Article L232-11 Code de commerce, and (iii) traceability of merchant-of-record settlement flows from Klarna BNPL or Shopify Payments to satisfy Article 150-0 B ter CGI on deferred payment arrangements (no material impact here as the BNPL counterparty is the deferred-payment provider, not the French vendor).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender, conversion ratio, retiming, or domiciliation requirement applies to export receipts in France. Since the liberalisation of 1988-1990 and the consolidation in CMF Article L151-2, all export proceeds in EUR and foreign currency are freely retainable in demand deposit or forex accounts. The SARL may keep USD/CNY settlement receivables offshore or convert them freely without Banque de France approval. The only residual obligation is statistical: reporting of cross-border payments related to exports, imports, and financial flows to the Banque de France (Balance of Payments statistics), by individual monthly declaration where the company's total international payment flows exceed the thresholds of the decree of 12 February 1987 (as revised), or under the 20-business-day cumulative declaration regime for amounts above the threshold; payments below these thresholds require only the company's own accounting records. For fast-fashion e-commerce, Shopify Payments and Klarna settlement flows are normally received under a single acquiring/BNPL contract and may be netted for BoP purposes, as expressly permitted by the Banque de France methodological note on payment institutions as reporting intermediaries.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech viability rating: HIGH for the operational payments layer. Qonto, Shine (Soshape), Revolut Business, and Wise Business are French/European PSD2 payment institutions or EMI credit institutions passported into France; they offer automated onboarding, French IBANs, MT103 reception, SEPA Instant issuance, and efficient receipt of Shopify Payments and Klarna BNPL settlements in EUR. LEGAL CONSTRAINT: they are not credit institutions undertaking banking transactions per CMF Article L311-1; they may not take retail deposits, most cannot issue commercial letters of credit, cannot grant ISDA/FBF derivative master access, and cannot act as a capital-escrow agent for a formal share-capital deposit under Article L223-7 Code de commerce (which requires funds to be held by a regulated credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations). An offshore EMI without either a French or a European passport has NO legal viability: the SARL may not lawfully rely on a non-EU EMI as its sole settlement rail without breaching the CMF L521-2 monopoly on payment services and the ACPR/Tracfin registration duty. Blueprint recommendation: engage a Tier-1 French bank for statutory capital escrow, commercial LC issuance, and FX hedging; retain a Fintech EMI as a secondary settlement account to accelerate Klarna/Shopify receipts and fast SEPA CTInst supplier payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Legal regime: CMF Article L561-5 (as amended by the 5th AML Directive transposition) imposes risk-based customer due diligence on credit institutions. Physical presence of the gérant (manager) and each UBO is not per se a statutory obligation, but it is the prevailing internal compliance practice of French Tier-1 banks for a non-resident-shareholder SARL. BNP Paribas, Société Générale, CACIB, and HSBC Continental Europe will in practice require at least one in-person interview at the local branch before opening, owing to (i) the ACPR inspection line on 'chains of delegation' in remote onboarding and (ii) the need to verify the gérant's identity under CMF Article L561-5-1. Remote opening is lawful since the COVID-era practice of ACPR non-opposition and is expressly available via video conference for French-resident corporate clients at most banks; for non-resident directors, a second documentary notarisation or a corresponding-bank verification is required. For ISIC 4791 fast-fashion e-commerce, the recommended route is one physical visit of the gérant to the chosen Tier-1 bank; remote-only fintech accounts (Qonto, Revolut) are fully legal as long as KYC data are captured through a dedicated video/ID-scan solution validated by the ACPR. There is no absolute remote-opening prohibition in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity — the bank cannot identify the natural persons ultimately owning or controlling the French SARL through the non-resident ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified statutory UBO register filed per Law No. 2018-898 (PACTE); notarised affidavit of the gérant listing each natural-person UBO above 25%; corporate chain-of-title with original share transfer deeds; passport or national ID of every UBO; equivalent UBO certificates from the jurisdictions of residence; statement self-certifying the absence of nominees and a written undertaking to notify the bank of any UBO change within 15 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concern on the capital injection by non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or fiscally attested parent-company accounts demonstrating distributable reserves; twelve-month accumulation bank statements of the shareholder(s); signed declaration of lawful origin (Article 324-1 and 324-2 Code pénal) included in the SARL's AML file; tax clearance certificates (US IRS Form 6166, German Freistellungsbescheinigung, or equivalent); notarised gift or loan agreement if the injection is a shareholder current account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce and BNPL third-party settlement risk — the bank flags Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments as payment intermediaries creating uncaptured merchant risk and refund-abuse exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Klarna merchant agreement and BNPL subledger showing merchant-of-record segregation; Shopify Payments terms and merchant agreement; settlement reconciliation files for the last three months proving that refunds are netted against identifiable sale transactions; documented refund policy; e-commerce dashboard admin-rights or log-in proof for the bank's risk officer; copies of GDPR (RGPD) data-processing annexes demonstrating third-party payment data protection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or sanctions exposure — customers or suppliers (fast-fashion imports from Bangladesh, China, Vietnam; consumers abroad) flagged against OFAC, EU, or OMT sanctions lists or high-risk third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal geo-blocking and export-control policy excluding sanctions-listed persons and territories; IP-country blocking and AVS/CVV verification report from the PSP; importer-of-record and sourcing compliance contracts with each supplier including UFLPA or forced-labour attestation; OFAC/EU sanctions-screening log generated by Shopify Radar or equivalent; Tracfin declaration certificate if any suspicious-transaction report was filed; staff AML training completion log.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency mismatch and permanent-establishment allegation — bank compliance deems the foreign-owned SARL at risk of being treated as a letterbox company or as having a foreign permanent establishment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French corporate tax residency certificate (Article 1220 CGI) and the SARL's K-bis extract; full organisational-chart memorandum proving substance in France (leased warehouse or fulfilment premises, payroll, e-commerce servers, local support team, distribution contracts); CRS/FATCA self-certification for each UBO and for the parent company; transfer-pricing documentation per Articles L13 AA and L13 B CGI and OECD Chapters I-III; copy of the annual profit-distribution resolution (AGM minutes) proving real French decision-making by the gérant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: the non-resident shareholder transfers cash to the SARL's Tier-1 escrow account in France. Euro-zone injection: SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001.001.09, Category Purpose TREA, or EBA intra-community code 'ACCA' for asset-to-liability transfer or cash contribution), credited via TARGET2 within T+1; SEPA Instant (SCTInst) may be used for amounts up to EUR 100,000 if the receiving bank subscribes to the SEPA Instant scheme. Non-EUR injection (USD or CNH) is remitted by SWIFT MT103 (field 72 containing the purpose code) into the SARL's multi-currency operational account and converted on trade date at best-execution. Verification duties: the receiving bank obtains an IBAN, a legalised K-bis extract, the SARL's articles of association, and the capital-deposit documentation; statutory compliance per Article L223-7 Code de commerce requires the funds to remain blocked with the bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts until the SARL is registered, with the release executed against the K-bis. FX-control reporting: the Banque de France requires an ex-post BoP statement within 20 business days for certain direct-investment flows or within the thresholds set by the decree of 12 February 1987, as updated; a standard French direct-investment declaration (CERFA form) is filed under the Banque de France's 12-series when the injection exceeds the relevant threshold. For injections below the threshold, the accounting entry under ledger code 101 'Capital' suffices. On the bank side, AML straight-through processing verifies compliance with CMF Article L561-2(2°) on the origin of funds; a pre-approved KYC dossier prevents holds on the MT103 or pain.001 payment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails selected: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for all European suppliers (fabric mills in Italy, Portugal, Poland) via EBICS batch submission T+1; (ii) SWIFT MT103 plus SWIFT gpi tracking for non-EUR trade settlements (USD to Bangladesh for garment letters of credit, CNH to Hong Kong accounts of Chinese sourcing agents, GBP to UK logistics hubs); (iii) documentary credit: SWIFT MT700 issued by the SARL's Tier-1 bank under UCP600 for fast-fashion supplier financing above EUR 50,000 per shipment, especially covering purchase-order financing from Bangladesh and Vietnam; (iv) open-account with supply-chain finance: a revolving confirmation or recommended-distribution facility via the bank's issuing counter, where the importer-finance repayments are matched to the SARL's disbursement schedule. The bank intermediates through SWIFT gpi, ISO 20022 pain.001 in EUR, and MT103 straight-through processing, ensuring compliance with the EU Cross-Border Payments Regulation (EU) 2021/1230 on fee transparency. For foreign-currency disbursements above EUR 100,000, outgoing MT103s are paired against executed FX forwards in a treasury pairing sheet to eliminate settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright FX forwards (vanilla bullet, flexible, up to 24 months) documented under the FBF Master Agreement 2018 (Fédération Bancaire Française) with an ISDA credit support annex where derivatives execution occurs via the Tier-1 bank's treasury desk
EUR/CNH forwards for Chinese sourcing payments, available as deliverable offshore renminbi (CNH) contracts with a 10% margin pre-deposit or a rollover line
FX swaps (Tom/Next, spot-forward, and double-swap-point structures) for temporary bridging of USD and CNH payment runs against USD and GBP collection fluctuations

EUR/USD and EUR/CNH vanilla FX options (call/put) and zero-premium cost-reversal structures for hedging purchase-order commitments beyond six months, documented under the ISDA/FBF 2018 Master Agreement approved by the bank's risk director

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) for capital-structure hedging of any medium-term shareholder-loan or bond-type refinancing, permitted as a class-2 derivative under CMF Article L211-1 and settled via TARGET2 or CLS where both leg currencies are CLS-eligible

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible under French law for exotic or inconvertible pairs such as EUR/BDT for Bangladesh coverage where onshore deliverable hedging is unavailable; however, given the free convertibility of the euro and the existence of deliverable CNH/USD markets, NDFs are recommended only as a residual instrument aligned with the final LC settlement rate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels) - filing with the trade registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval of annual accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit with the greffe within 1 month of approval and no later than 7 months after year-end (e.g., 31 July 2026 for 31 December 2025 year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 4,000 (approx. USD 4,300) for legal entities (Art. L.232-23 C.com.); failure for two consecutive years may lead to judicial strike-off and dissolution at the request of the public prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Liasse Fiscale no. 2065 and related schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, e-filing by the second business day following 1 May (e.g., 4 May 2026); otherwise, within 3 months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of net tax due; 40% after a formal demand; 80% for deliberate omission; plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month. Tax authorities can issue an excise assessment (d'office) and require company dissolution in severe cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following at the balance-sheet date (Art. L.232-2, D.232-1 C. com.): total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. The obligation also applies to controlling or controlled entities meeting consolidated thresholds, or upon shareholder demand holding at least 10% of shares.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG), based on Articles L.123-12 et seq. of the Commercial Code; EU-endorsed IFRS is permitted solely for consolidated accounts, not for the SARL's statutory individual statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO 'no-change' confirmation. The beneficial-owner declaration is filed with the RCS upon incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any share transfer or direct/indirect ownership change (crossing 25%, 50%, 75% thresholds or control). The manager should review the UBO register and share-register entries at each annual general meeting and make amendment filings if ownership events occurred during the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Minute Book (Registre des Décisions et Procès-Verbaux des Assemblées Générales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 650 (EUR 220 - 600) for a commercial domiciliation address and corporate agent services in France.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,200 - 5,500 (EUR 2,000 - 5,000) for a statutory audit conducted by a commissaire aux comptes for a small or medium-sized SARL; no audit fee is incurred if the entity is below the legal audit thresholds and does not require a voluntary auditor.
